title: Effectiveness of Deep Water Running on Improving Cardiorespiratory Fitness, Physical Function and Quality of Life: A Systematic Review
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (MDPI)
claims: The systematic review compared deep water running (DWR) with land-based training, no active exercise, and other modalities for cardiorespiratory fitness, physical function and quality of life.
Five studies found similar effects of DWR and land-based training on VO2max; in athletic populations the standardized mean difference for VO2max ranged from 0.06 to 0.10.

DWR may produce lower physiological responses than land running, including lower VO2max and maximal heart rate, although the stimulus may still suffice for supplementary training with reduced orthopedic trauma.
DWR is non-weight-bearing; its biomechanics compared with land running remain unclear, and muscle activation differs between distal leg and proximal thigh muscles.
The review concludes that the small number of studies, heterogeneity and varied participant types limit stronger conclusions, and further research is needed for targeted prescriptions.
